content:
anya: quick async — proposal: normalize message.role to lowercase in chat/completions responses and add a \"role_normalized\" field for streaming deltas. also introduce a small set of stream.event values for tool calls (e.g., \"tool_call\", \"tool_return\"). will this break SDKs or downstream code?

sam: do you mean only in server responses, or also in the request/messages payload we accept?

anya: only responses/deltas we emit. we won't change user-sent message shape. goal is to make consumers' equality checks simpler (no case juggling).

leo: heads up — several older SDKs do literal string equality against roles (e.g., \"Assistant\", \"User\"). lowercasing will break those. we should provide a migration strategy. options: add an explicit \"role_normalized\" field for a deprecation window, or include a response header like `X-RI-role-normalization: true` to gate behavior per-client.

maria: +1 on a migration window. suggest making it opt-in query param or header first (e.g., `?role_normalization=lowercase` or `X-RI-Role-Norm: true`) then flip default after one major SDK bump. also add integration tests to convo-compat suite.

anya: proposal for rollout (rough):
1) add `role_normalized` to all responses AND to streaming delta events (no change to existing `role`).
2) add optional header `X-RI-Role-Norm: lowercase` that, when present, also updates `role` to lowercase in emitted events (for canaries).
3) after 8 weeks and SDK updates, flip default, then deprecate `role_normalized` field after 3 months.

leo: sounds sensible. streaming nuance: some clients treat partial deltas (role changes mid-stream) specially. we'll need to ensure deltas include `role_normalized` from the start of the turn. otherwise reassembly tests will fail.

anya: good catch. plan: on streaming start event we emit a small metadata chunk with both fields. example: 

```
{ \"type\": \"message_start\", \"role\": \"Assistant\", \"role_normalized\": \"assistant\" }
```

and regular chunk: 
```
{ \"type\": \"message_delta\", \"role\": \"Assistant\", \"role_normalized\": \"assistant\", \"delta\": \"Hello\" }
```

sam: will run SDK parsing tests once the server PR lands. quick check: do we need to change toolcall payloads? order of `tool` args has bitten us before.

anya: no change to tool arg ordering in the payload — just add a `stream.event` value for explicit toolcall signals in the streaming path: e.g., `stream.event = \"tool_call\"` with a `tool_payload` obj. keep existing `function_call` compat fields.

sdk-bot: sdk-ci: compatibility scan results (preliminary) — node-sdk: 12 failures (role equality), python-sdk: 11 failures (parse tests), go-sdk: 0 failures. Logging reports attached in CI.

maria: ok, tasks: leo — server PR to add `role_normalized` + header, include streaming start/delta examples. sam — SDKs: add tolerant parse code + feature flag support. i'll add integration tests to convo-compat and schedule a canary run. i'll also own the deprecation timeline doc.

leo: ack :thumbsup: i'll draft PR, will include unit tests for delta ordering and role fields. ETA: EOD tomorrow.

sam: i'll patch node & python SDKs, add opt-in header handling and warn logs for old equality checks. ETA: 2 days.

maria: i'll add tests and coordinate canary (canary-3). ping me for review.

infra-bot: deploybot: canary cluster deploy started (canary-3) for branch/role-norm (build 2026.1766.1).

anya: thanks all — small doc note: update migration guide / changelog and call out streaming delta behavior. once canary looks good we'll open the SDK PR checklist. :tada:

leo: minor nit — make sure we don't rely on `role_normalized` in service-to-service internals until after flip. some autorouters assume case-sensitive match.

anya: noted. i'll add a config flag to prevent internal services from switching until cutover.

sam: cool — i'll add a test in sdk-compat that validates both `role` and `role_normalized` present.

maria: moving this to async review — if no objections by EOD Friday we'll start canary next week.

anya: thanks everyone. tagging @sam @leo @maria for followups.
